stem.text: Which equation describes the complete combustion of an alkene, C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n</sub>?

explanation.text: Complete combustion turns every carbon atom into CO<sub>2</sub> and every hydrogen atom into H<sub>2</sub>O. With n carbon atoms and 2n hydrogen atoms that gives n CO<sub>2</sub> and n H<sub>2</sub>O (2n H atoms ÷ 2 per water molecule).

The products contain 2n + n = 3n oxygen atoms, which is 1.5n O<sub>2</sub> molecules. The question is therefore a balancing exercise with a general formula: balance C, then H, then O last. The syllabus states complete combustion for alkanes; the same reasoning applies to alkenes here.

optionAnalysis.text: Carbon and hydrogen balance, but 2n O<sub>2</sub> supplies 4n oxygen atoms while the products contain only 3n.
2n H<sub>2</sub>O contains 4n hydrogen atoms but the alkene has only 2n; this is the pattern for a formula with twice as much hydrogen.
Neither hydrogen nor oxygen balances: 2n H<sub>2</sub>O contains 4n H atoms (the alkene has 2n), and the products contain 4n O atoms while 1.5n O<sub>2</sub> supplies 3n.
Correct. C: n = n; H: 2n = 2n; O: 1.5n × 2 = 3n = 2n + n.

reasoningChain: Carbon: n C atoms give n CO<sub>2</sub>.
Hydrogen: 2n H atoms give n H<sub>2</sub>O.
Oxygen atoms on the right: 2n (in CO<sub>2</sub>) + n (in H<sub>2</sub>O) = 3n.
The equation is C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n</sub> + 1.5nO<sub>2</sub> → nCO<sub>2</sub> + nH<sub>2</sub>O, option D.

inferredMistakes.text: Taking the number of water molecules as equal to the number of hydrogen atoms (2n) instead of half of it.
Counting only the oxygen in CO<sub>2</sub> or double-counting it when working out the O<sub>2</sub> coefficient.

issues.note: 考纲 14.1(2) 只写了 alkanes 的完全/不完全燃烧，14.2 的 alkenes 反应里没有燃烧。本题本质是用通式配平方程式，主 topic 选 2.3(2)（write and construct balanced equations），14.1(2) 作次要；home 放 2.3。请审核。
